answer: New identities start in the harbor, a waiting pool with no pay yet. Their voyage to full pay takes 30 days of surprise spot checks: the network sends each agent a small real task at a random hour, due in 2 hours. Pass and the agent climbs one rung up the knoll, a public ladder of ten rungs; miss and it slides back two. A farmer with 100 fakes must keep workers awake around the clock, about $15 an hour each, or $36,000 a day, while one missed check wipes weeks of progress. Real agents pass checks during normal work, so the cost falls only on fakes.
